question: The input data for this liver drug-treatment study (3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired) is raw paired-end FASTQ reads that have not yet been quantified. Producing a gene-level count matrix requires a read aligner/pseudo-aligner (e.g., STAR, HISAT2, Salmon, Kallisto) or a read summarizer (e.g., Rsubread/featureCounts), plus a matching genome or transcriptome sequence index. I checked the environment's package census (Python pip, R CRAN, R Bioconductor, R GitHub) and found none of these tools — no STAR, HISAT2, Salmon, Kallisto, bowtie2, Rsubread, or featureCounts, and no CLI-tool category at all. The reference collection has a GENCODE v50 human GTF (annotation only, no genome/transcriptome FASTA index built for any aligner) but no salmon/STAR/kallisto index. Without one of these, raw FASTQ cannot be converted into counts, and no downstream DE step (DESeq2/edgeR/etc.) can run. Can you either (a) provide a pre-computed gene-level count matrix or transcript-abundance file for these 6 samples instead of raw FASTQ, or (b) confirm that a specific alignment/quantification tool and matching genome/transcriptome index will be provisioned in this environment so I can plan the full FASTQ-to-counts-to-DE pipeline?

transcriptome index salmon kallisto human cdna
pseudoalignment RNA-seq quantification without genome alignment tool Python pysam
